sections.name: ROUTES
sections.title: No money language on each route
sections.what: Loads each public route, reads its visible text, and fails if money words appear outside disclaimers or if payment-style markers are present.
sections.why: Catches money wording that a developer might add to any page.
sections.watch_out: The route list must include every public page, or new pages will skip the check.

summary: Browser test that scans the rendered text of every public page for money language and checks no payment-style images or markers appear.
purpose: Enforces the product rule that the app contains no money features on any page a user can see.
why: The app must not look like a betting or payments product, so a page-by-page check on real rendered text guards against drift.
how: For each route in the list, it loads the page, waits for network activity to quiet down, reads the visible body text, and passes it to the shared money-term audit. It expects no hits. It also expects no image or element whose name or attribute suggests a payment code or payment marker.
inputs: The route list and the rendered page text.
outputs: Pass or fail per route, with the matched term and context on failure.
risks: New pages must be added to the route list, or they go unchecked. The check only sees text on the rendered page, not text hidden behind interaction.
debug: Read the failing term and context from the report, then decide whether it is a real money word or an allowed disclaimer. Fix the copy or the audit exception.
